title: Quantix Systems — capacity renegotiation + EU onboarding check-in
next_steps: Redwood to send updated proposal with EU region pricing and PO term options
Quantix to confirm expected steady-state qps and peak day multipliers by 2026-05-20
Schedule technical benchmark with Quantix SRE and Redwood SE (Jon) week of 2026-05-25
action_items: Jon Patel: run 2-model perf benchmarks (generation+embedding) on eu-west region and share logs (due: 2026-05-27)
Maya Rosen: prepare revised commercial with 12-month extension and 20% reserved capacity tier pricing (due: 2026-05-19)
Marco Ruiz: share PO process and legal contact details (due: 2026-05-18)
Darya Petrov: provide internal traffic profile and token distribution samples (due: 2026-05-20)
summary: Renewal/expansion check-in focused on adding EU region to Dedicated pool, discussing uplift in reserved capacity for H2, and aligning commercial term options. Customer requested benchmarks in eu-west, clarified procurement timeline, and asked for SOC/ISO attestation copy. Agreed next steps to deliver revised quote and run tech perf tests.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Rosen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're aiming to run 45 minutes; quick rollcall?
00:07 Liam O'Connor: Liam here, hi. Darya on my side, Marco and Sofia also dialed in.
00:13 Maya Rosen: Awesome. Jon from our SE team and Priya our CSM are with me. Quick agenda: sizing for H2, EU region onboarding timeline, and commercial options for extending the commitment.
00:25 Marco Ruiz: Sounds good. From procurement side we just need to know PO timing and whether pricing changes with regions.
00:30 Jon Patel: Quick note, when we say EU region we mean eu-west-1 on the current infra; we can also support eu-central but latency/availability profiles differ.
00:42 Darya Petrov: Right, latency's the big one. Our EU customers expect sub-200ms median for chat flows. Are those SLOs realistic on the Dedicated pools?
00:51 Jon Patel: Yes, with the reserved GPU pools we typically see median token latency under 120ms for the 8k context gen model we benchmarked. That said, real world depends on batching and prefix cache — I want to run a region-specific run with your token distribution.
01:08 Liam O'Connor: We have two peaks: steady steady-state ~150 qps embedding calls, and a marketing day peak that maybe 4x. We want to size for predictable performance and avoid over-commit spend.
01:22 Maya Rosen: Totally—so options: increase reserved capacity with autoscaling burst, or keep current reserved and rely on burst credits; both have different price points. For renewal we can present a 12 or 24 month term with tiered discounts.
01:35 Marco Ruiz: For contract extension, 12 months is easier to get approved quickly. Can you do a 10-15% discount if we bump reserved from X to 2.5X?
01:42 Maya Rosen: I can draft that as an option. We offered 12% at prior renewal; for 2.5x reserved we can look at 18% on committed usage, plus a lower per-token overage rate. I will confirm with finance.
01:54 Sofia Nguyen: Quick technical Q — when you say reserved capacity, is that per-model or shared pool across models? We run a mix of generation+embedding variants.
02:01 Jon Patel: It's a dedicated GPU pool that can be partitioned by model routing. Shared pool routing is common — you pin critical models and let others be routed to compatible variants. We're mindful of KV cache coherence when models share hardware.
02:18 Darya Petrov: You mentioned KV cache — we've seen cache misses causing spikes. Can you share how cache cold-start is handled during failover?
02:26 Jon Patel: Sure — runtime keeps prefix/KV caches warm for pinned replicas; during failover we have fallback policies and warm-up heuristics. There can be a short degradation window; that's why we recommend canary routing in new regions.
02:40 Marco Ruiz: On compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and an ISO attestation. Also, does the EU region satisfy data residency for logs?
02:49 Priya Singh: We can share SOC2 and ISO docs. For logs/data: for Dedicated we can configure region-local retention and KMS keys; we also support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
03:03 Liam O'Connor: Great. Procurement timeline: we'll need the commercial by Wednesday so legal can review and get sign-off before end of May.
03:11 Maya Rosen: We'll aim to get revised commercial by 2026-05-19. Jon will run a eu-west benchmark and share results by 2026-05-27.
03:20 Sofia Nguyen: Are there any pitfalls we should know for onboarding the eu-west cluster — e.g., model licensing or quantization differences?
03:28 Jon Patel: Models are the same, but quantization/ops can vary by kernel availability in region. We'll verify kernel set and replicate our quantization profile; if we need special builds we'll flag that early.
03:40 Darya Petrov: For the benchmark, what artifacts do you need from us?
03:44 Jon Patel: Token distribution samples, representative prompts, and a test service account key — ideally a short window of traffic replay. Also expected qps and peak multiplier.
03:55 Liam O'Connor: I'll coordinate that with Darya and share by 2026-05-20.
04:00 Marco Ruiz: On pricing, any chance to lock today's pricing for 24 months if we sign a 2-year?
04:07 Maya Rosen: Finance sometimes allows price protections; 24-month commits get the best protection. We'll model a 12-month and 24-month option in the proposal.
04:15 Marco Ruiz: Also, we prefer net-30 invoicing; is that acceptable?
04:19 Maya Rosen: Net-30 is fine; we'll note that in the commercial.
04:23 Question (unlabeled): How do credits for burst capacity appear on invoices?
04:27 Priya Singh: Burst credits are usually consumed before overages; we'll show a line-item breakdown in the invoice and in the console's token-level cost view.
04:36 Sofia Nguyen: One more — latency SLOs, do you offer SLA credits for missed p99?
04:40 Maya Rosen: For Dedicated with SLA add-on, yes we have uptime and latency targets with credit structure; I'll attach SLA doc.
04:48 Darya Petrov: For the benchmark run, can you simulate our worst-case payloads? We have some long conversational contexts (8k tokens).
04:55 Jon Patel: We will; can we confirm model size and context? Sofia?
04:59 Sofia Nguyen: We'll send details: 8k contexts for some flows, mostly gen model size medium family.
05:04 Maya Rosen: Great. To recap next steps — Maya to send revised commercial by 2026-05-19, Jon to run benchmarks and share logs by 2026-05-27, Quantix to provide traffic and procurement details by 2026-05-20.
05:18 Liam O'Connor: That matches our notes. Anything else?
05:22 Marco Ruiz: Legal will also want redwood's DPA and data flow diagrams — can you include those?
05:28 Priya Singh: Yes we'll attach DPA and a high level flow diagram.
05:32 Maya Rosen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with attachments and the proposal.
05:36 End of call
notes: Customer prioritized EU data residency and deterministic performance for H2. Commercial negotiation centered on reserved capacity uplift and term length (12 v 24 months). SE needs traffic artifacts to run accurate eu-west benchmarks. Procurement needs PO/legal contacts and prefers net-30.
